page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v7 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external Premium Storage options. There are no onboard GPUs, which limits its applicability for hardware-accelerated graphics or heavy deep learning training workloads. However, the CPU features built-in hardware acceleration for cryptography, such as AES and SHA extensions, and integer bit manipulation.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU extended instructions test placing in the top 25%. The PassMark CPU score and database operations benchmark both rank in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks consistently perform in the top 25%. For language model workloads, the CPU's AMX instructions support strong prompt processing speeds in the top 25% tier, though text generation speeds remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64s_v7 offers a high-density resource profile suitable for enterprise workloads that require balanced compute and memory without the overhead of local storage maintenance. It is suited for relational database management systems, multi-threaded decompression tasks, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.

Utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 system features 32 physical cores and a 480 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on external Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks show top 10% tier results in PassMark CPU and database operations, alongside top 25% tier results in multi-core stress-ng, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic execution. The processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) enable strong prompt processing speeds for large language models, though text generation remains average. This resource profile is suited for enterprise database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and static web serving.
